summary.headline: Yasho Q4 FY26 revenue rose 33% YoY to INR246.7 crore with EBITDA margin at 18.1%; FY27 utilisation target is 75%+.
summary.overview: Consolidated FY26 revenue reached INR830 crore (up 22.7% YoY) with EBITDA of INR144 crore and margin of 17.4%, while Q4 revenue was INR246.72 crore (up 33%) with EBITDA of INR44.71 crore at 18.1%. Growth was entirely volume-led (FY26 volume up 33%), with management saying prices were under pressure until late March when 10-15% price increases started, mostly effective from April. Management guided to FY27 utilisation above 75% (from about 60% in FY26), volume growth of 35-45%, and a FY28 revenue target of INR1,500 crore tied to a 15-year long-term contract with INR51.4 crore advance. Leverage fell to 3.75x debt-to-EBITDA from 4.70x, and INR23.3 crore of FY27 liabilities were prepaid.

segments.name: Industrial Chemicals
segments.commentary: Contributed 87% of revenue in both Q4 and full FY26 and is the key growth driver; management says all volume growth came from the industrial segment, with a slight dip on the consumer side.

segments.name: Exports
segments.commentary: Accounted for 62% of FY26 revenue; Americas demand improved in Q4 as tariffs moderated, and Europe is seeing some slowdown. Management is also starting to enter Asia.

guidance_outlook: FY27 utilisation target above 75% (from above 60% in FY26); management also cited 70-75% and about 15 percentage points of utilisation uplift.
FY27 volume growth of 35-45% (clarified after several restatements); EBITDA margin expected at least 2-3 percentage points above FY26, with a stated aim of about 20%.

FY28 revenue target of INR1,500 crore, supported by asset utilisation of 85-90%, the MNC long-term contract going into commercial operation from early FY28, and FY27 capacity additions; management says margins will be maintained.
FY27 capex of INR125 crore, fully funded by internal accruals and entirely at Pakhajan; management says none of it relates to the long-term contract.
Working capital to fall to about 170-175 days over 6-12 months from about 190 days.
Debt-to-EBITDA comfort zone of about 2.5x; absolute debt may rise while the ratio falls.
capex_capacity: FY26 capex INR75 crore: about INR25 crore R&D, INR40-42 crore Pakhajan, INR7-8 crore Vapi.
R&D facility completed October 2025 and fully operational.

Pakhajan has 2 production buildings built, with room for 4 more to be started one by one as demand ramps; a special project of about INR90 crore is running, and a further INR100 crore Pakhajan capex is under consideration.
Utilisation was above 60% in FY26 (60-62% through March); management declined to give plant-wise utilisation.
Management was unsure of the current total capacity figure, which was stated as 12,000 to 32,000 (unit not specified).
demand_pricing: Price increases of about 10-15% versus the pre-war base; these took effect only in the last 10 days of March and from April, as contracts were fixed quarterly or half-yearly until then.
About 40% of revenue comes from regular customers on quarterly or six-monthly pricing; about 60% is spot or relationship-based.
Pricing pressure and margin pressure through FY26, with product mix shifted away from low-margin products.
Import delays of 8-12 weeks versus 3-4 weeks normally; US export transit has risen to 60-70 days from 25 days.
Sulfur availability is challenging but available; solvents and sulfur-based chemistries show strong price volatility.
Chinese competitors described as very strong and aggressive in lubricant additives and industrial chemicals.
India-EU FTA expected around early January; Yasho has a European team about one year old.

qa_highlights.question: Is the INR1,500 crore FY28 target visible and what drives it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management cited utilisation rising to 85-90% by FY28, the special project coming on stream in FY28, and new rubber and lube molecules; the visibility is partly customer commitments made on the table.

qa_highlights.question: Is the company moving into CDMO?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Yasho is not a CDMO and will not serve small-volume API-type orders of 20-100 metric tons. It will work with large-volume customers, with Pakhajan designed for 500-1,000 metric tons minimum per molecule.

qa_highlights.question: What is the working capital outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Days have fallen from 215-216 in FY25 to about 190; the target is 170-175 over 6-12 months. Debtors are flat, and stock was useful in the supply crisis.

qa_highlights.question: How much of the FY27 volume growth is from price versus volume?
qa_highlights.answer: Management measures growth in volume terms, and says price increases only started in late March and April 2026. Currency gains are largely offset by imported raw materials.

qa_highlights.question: Does Yasho make its own formulations?
qa_highlights.answer: No. Yasho only makes pure chemicals and does not compete with its formulating customers.

qa_highlights.question: Is the MNC project capex included in the FY27 capex?
qa_highlights.answer: No. The INR125 crore FY27 capex is separate; the share of capex attributable to the MNC project is zero.

risks_watch: Supply chain disruption from the Middle East: import delays, raw material shortages, and high petrochemical prices; management says high inventory has offset this so far.
Chinese competition in lubricant additives and industrial chemicals.
Europe slowdown and the timing of the India-EU FTA (expected around early January).
Working capital reduction to 170-175 days depends on raw material availability.
Ramp to 75% utilisation and the FY28 INR1,500 crore target depend on the MNC contract and new molecules; each new molecule targeted at INR50 crore or more.
Ability to hold EBITDA margin as the customer price increases pass through, given management says costs cannot be fully passed on.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volume and utilisation targets and on the FY28 ambition, but cautious and evasive on pricing outlook, raw material supply and the timing of new molecules. Management repeatedly declined to give plant-level data, product breakdowns or forward price views, and said it did not know when prices would normalise.
key_quotes: Consolidated revenue reached INR830 crores, up 22.7% year-on-year, while EBITDA stood at INR144 crores with margin improving to 17.4%, supported by product mix, operating leverage and cost optimization.
The company always measures growth in terms of volume.
We are purely chemical producers. We are in B2B. We are not in B2C segment.
Yasho is not governed for the CDMO kind of work.

adds.what: Pakhajan plant: 4 further production buildings to be started one by one as demand ramps; ~INR90 crore special project running
15-year MNC long-term contract going into commercial operation from early FY28 (supports INR1,500 crore FY28 revenue target)

growth.why: Management guides FY27 volume growth of 35-45% and utilisation above 75% (from ~60%), backed by spare capacity at Pakhajan, a INR51.4 crore advance on a 15-year MNC contract starting early FY28, and an FY28 revenue target of INR1,500 crore; the call gave no plant-wise or unit-specified capacity figures, so backing is only partial.
